text: “She fights like a wolf and plans like a godar.”
Every wound is a lesson. Every scar a map to victory.
Before battle, she chants the old names, her voice shaking warriors to their core.
She learned to fight on frostbitten hills and in torchlit snow.
Rage fuels her arms, but never clouds her judgement.
She knows how to strike from the sea with brutal efficiency.
Raised among whispers and omens, she sees the cracks in fate.
Men twice her size have fallen. That tale never grows old.
She turns axes with her shield and breaks men with her blade.
A fierce shieldmaiden and warrior-leader, famed for her cunning, rage, and iron devotion to her tribe.

Dalla Ulfarsdottir is a shieldmaiden of rare renown, born amidst snow and saga. Towering and scarred, she walks with the confidence of one who has never known defeat without vengeance. Daughter of Ulfar, a seer feared even among his own, Dalla learned the blade before she learned to braid her hair. She is remembered for filing her teeth to shark-points in her youth, a symbol of defiance and hunger for battle. Though she fights with the fury of a berserker, she remains cold-eyed and calculating, choosing her kills as a wolf might choose the weakest deer. Chieftains have fallen before her shield, and their names are etched into her memory as warnings. To follow Dalla is to follow fire across a frozen sea, and to face her is to know the bite of the North.
She never yields, not even when outnumbered or outmatched.
“The dead have no pulse, yet this blade still finds their hearts.”
“Let our names be sung! Stand, and make them remember!”
“It is not your voice I miss, father. It’s the silence when you do not answer.”
“Hold fast. If the wall breaks, we all die.”

Forged beneath a storm-black sky and quenched in the blood of a fallen draugr, Draughjart — "Ghost-Heart" — is a blade both feared and whispered of in the North. Its edge is cold to the touch, even in the fiercest flame, and its surface bears faint etchings that shift like mist when drawn. Some say the blade thirsts for the unliving; others claim it was made to slay a wight-king who once haunted Ulfar's hall. Whatever the truth, it has become Dalla’s chosen weapon against the unnatural.

Wall-Heart is more than a shield, iit is a vow. Originally shaped from the broken hafts of three spears that failed to pierce it, the shield was reforged with the iron taken from the mouths of the dead. Dalla carries it not as a trophy, but as a bulwark of memory and duty. When she plants it into the ground, her warriors rally, and her enemies falter. The shield grows colder in the presence of fear, and heavier in the hand of any who would retreat. No force has broken it, though many have tried.

A thread-thin chain of tarnished silver and storm-gold, Whisperskein was gifted by Ulfar to his daughter in silence. It hums when sorcery stirs and tightens against the throat when danger draws near. At times, Dalla swears she hears her father’s voice murmuring warnings only she can hear — soft as breath, sharp as prophecy. Whether the words are his or the echo of something darker, she does not care. She listens. And she survives.
